topic.title: Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act 2026

subtopics.title: Passage and timeline
subtopics.summary: The United States enacted the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 after House passage and Senate approval. The House voted 262 to 159 on 16 September, and the President signed the Act into law on 18 September 2026. The measure matters for India because India remains one of the major buyers of Russian crude.

subtopics.title: Key provisions
subtopics.summary: The Act authorises tariffs of up to 100% on the five largest purchasers of Russian oil and natural gas, a substantial reduction from the 500% original proposal. It also authorises tariffs of up to 500% on Russian-origin goods, subject to specified exceptions. A 180-day review cycle for relevant purchasers and defined conditions for ending the sanctions framework complete its core design.

subtopics.title: Legal permanence and US trade tools
subtopics.summary: The earlier 25% punitive tariff on India was based on an Executive Order, and in February 2026 the U.S. Supreme Court struck down the broader tariff regime that included it. The new measure has been passed by Congress, signed and converted into federal law, which gives it greater legal permanence. A presidential waiver under the Act requires formal justification to Congress.

subtopics.title: Global and India implications
subtopics.summary: The measure illustrates growing use of secondary sanctions and tariff instruments to influence the behaviour of third countries. It could change global oil trade patterns as major buyers diversify suppliers and reconfigure energy contracts. For India, Russia is the top oil supplier, so potential tariffs complicate bilateral trade while India balances strategic autonomy with its energy interests.

quizzes.title: Act provisions check
quizzes.passage: Russia's war in Ukraine has prompted the United States to enact a law that increases economic pressure on Russia, while also extending and strengthening certain sanctions against Iran. The statute, named after Lindsey O. Graham, is built around criteria that decide which buyers of Russian energy fall within its reach. The law gives the executive branch several trade tools, including tariffs on the largest buyers of Russian oil and natural gas and tariffs on goods of Russian origin. Because the list of relevant buyers can change over time, the law provides for a periodic review carried out by the trade representative. Countries that rely only lightly on Russian gas, and that are actively cutting their imports, may qualify for a special exception. The framework's effect is also conditional, since it may be affected if Russia meets certain conditions linked to peace in Ukraine and to the stance of the Ukrainian government. For India, the measure is especially relevant because the country remains one of the major buyers of Russian crude, so Indian policymakers must weigh energy security against trade relations with the United States. Its economic effects would depend on how the tariffs are applied and how buyers respond.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): India is significantly affected by the Act even though the law names no individual country.
Reason (R): Its criteria place major buyers of Russian crude like India within its regulatory scope.

questions.explanation: The Act names no country, but its criteria place major buyers such as India and China within its scope, which explains why India is affected.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Act:
I. It authorises tariffs of up to 500% on Russian-origin goods, subject to specified exceptions.
II. The U.S. Trade Representative must reassess relevant purchasers on a 90-day review cycle.
III. A country importing less than 15% of its natural gas from Russia can qualify for an exception if it takes significant steps to reduce such imports.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement II is wrong because the review cycle is 180 days, not 90 days.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about the Act are correct?
A. The House of Representatives passed the Act by 262 votes to 159 on 16 September 2026.
B. The Act extends the Iran Sanctions Act of 1996 through 2031.
C. The President signed the Act into law on 16 September 2026.
D. The Act names India directly as a country subject to its tariffs.
questions.explanation: Statements A and B are correct, while C is wrong because the signing was on 18 September and D is wrong because the Act names no individual country.

quizzes.title: Legal tools check
quizzes.passage: Trade measures linked to Russian energy purchases raise questions about how long they will last. A tariff that rests only on a decision by the executive can be challenged in court, and courts can strike down a wide trade regime built on such a decision. A measure that has been passed by the legislature and signed into federal law carries greater legal permanence. American trade policy also relies on older statutes that give the government tools to respond to foreign practices. One of these allows the trade representative to examine unfair conduct by other countries. Another permits restrictions on imports when they are seen as a risk to national security. The government has also used tariffs on certain imported metals, and it has applied tariffs connected with goods produced through forced labour. For a country like India, such instruments matter because they change the cost of exports and make trade talks more complicated. Officials and businesses often watch these tools closely because a single measure can affect many sectors at once. Understanding the legal route behind each tariff helps explain why some measures last longer than others.
